**Analysis of the test image:**

The test image shows a single broad tomato leaf with:
- **Overall dark green** coloration with **yellowish-green mottled patches** on the leaf surface
- **Sandy/beige background** texture
- No discrete spots, lesions, or necrotic areas
- No white powdery coating
- No leaf curling or cupping
- Somewhat wrinkled/stippled leaf texture with uneven coloration

**Comparison with reference images:**

| Class | Match? | Key distinguishing features |
|---|---|---|
| Spider_Mites | **Strong** | Identical sandy background, same broad leaf, same dark green + yellowish mottled pattern |
| Mosaic_Virus | Partial | Similar mottling but different background, more obvious light/dark alternation |
| Tomato_Mosaic_Virus | Partial | Similar mottling, but darker background, leaves smaller/more serrated |
| TYLCV | No | Requires distinct leaf curling/cupping |
| Powdery_Mildew | No | Would show white/gray powdery coating |
| Early_Blight | No | Requires dark concentric lesions with yellow halos |
| Verticillium_Wilt | No | Shows severe yellowing/browning and wilting |
| Leaf_Mold | No | Pale bleached appearance, different texture |

The test image is a near-perfect visual match to the Spider_Mites reference images: same sandy background, same broad leaf morphology, same characteristic dark green with diffuse yellowish bronzing/mottling caused by spider mite feeding damage (stippling).
